sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: How far away terrain is rendered, in chunks. Shorter distances render less terrain, improving frame rates.
sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: The minimum brightness of the world. Raising it makes dark areas appear brighter without affecting areas that are already well lit.
sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: The maximum scale factor for the user interface. With "Auto", the largest scale that fits your screen is always used.
sodium.options.fullscreen.tooltip: Displays the game in fullscreen mode, when supported.
sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: Synchronizes the frame rate with your monitor's refresh rate for a smoother image, at the cost of a little input latency. May reduce performance on slower systems.
sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Caps the frame rate. A lower cap can reduce battery drain and system load while multitasking. Ignored while VSync is enabled, unless set below your display's refresh rate.
sodium.options.view_bobbing.tooltip: Sways the camera while walking. Players prone to motion sickness may prefer to turn this off.
sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: The default graphics quality. It controls some legacy options, and any option below that is set to "Default" follows this setting.
sodium.options.cloud_height.name: Cloud Height
sodium.options.cloud_height.tooltip: The altitude at which clouds are rendered.
sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: The quality level used for rendering clouds. Despite the "Fast" and "Fancy" labels, the performance difference is negligible.
sodium.options.weather_quality.name: Weather Quality
sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: How far away weather effects such as rain and snow are rendered.
sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodium.options.leaves_quality.tooltip: Whether leaves are rendered as see-through (Fancy) or opaque (Fast).
sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Enables smooth lighting and shading of blocks. This slightly increases chunk load and update times, but does not affect frame rates.
sodium.options.biome_blend.name: Biome Blend Radius
sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The area, in blocks, over which biome colors are blended. The default is 5x5. Larger values noticeably increase chunk load and update times for diminishing visual gains.
sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: Renders simple shadows beneath mobs and other entities.
sodium.options.entity_shadow_distance.to: How far from the camera entity shadows remain visible. Higher values may slightly reduce performance.
sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: Darkens the edges of the screen in dark areas for a more dramatic look.
sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: The number of mipmaps used for block textures. Higher values make distant blocks look smoother, but can hurt performance with resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodium.options.chunk_fade.name: Chunk Fade
sodium.options.chunk_fade.tooltip: How long newly loaded chunks take to fade in. Set to zero to make chunks appear instantly.
sodium.options.brighten_fireworks.name: Brighten Fireworks
sodium.options.brighten_fireworks.toolti: Brightens firework particles so they stand out better against the sky.
sodium.options.better_skies.name: Better Skies
sodium.options.better_skies.tooltip: Enables the sky rendering improvements from the MCPatcher mod, including custom resource-pack skyboxes.
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Chunk Update Threads
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: The number of threads used for building and sorting chunks. More threads speed up chunk loading and updates, but may cost some frame-time smoothness. The default is a good fit for most machines.
sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.name: Chunk Updates
sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.toolt: "Deferred" never waits for nearby chunk updates, giving the best frame rates but letting block changes lag behind visually. "Immediate" blocks the frame until updates finish, eliminating visual lag. "Soon" is a compromise that allows at most one frame of lag.
sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: Skips rendering block faces that point away from the camera. This removes a large amount of hidden geometry very early and greatly improves performance. If a resource pack shows holes in blocks, try disabling this.
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Use Fog Occlusion
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: Skips rendering chunks that are fully hidden by fog. The gain is largest when fog is heavy, such as underwater, but it can cause minor artifacts where the sky meets the fog.
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use Entity Culling
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: Skips rendering entities that are inside the camera's view but hidden within non-visible chunks. This reuses the visibility data already computed for chunk rendering, so it adds no overhead.
sodium.options.smart_cull.name: Use Smart Culling
sodium.options.smart_cull.tooltip: Uses a smarter occlusion-culling algorithm to skip hidden chunks. In caves and built-up areas this can give a large FPS boost.
sodium.options.vbos.tooltip: Uses Vertex Buffer Objects (VBOs) for rendering. This improves performance on most systems, but may cause visual issues on very old hardware.
sodium.options.quad_splitting.name: Perfect Translucency
sodium.options.quad_splitting.tooltip: Splits translucent block geometry so that intersecting or oddly shaped blocks, such as waterlogged stained-glass panes, sort correctly. "Safe" limits how much extra geometry may be generated in extreme cases; "Unlimited" removes that limit.
sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to: For debugging only. Keeps the staging buffer persistently mapped so unnecessary memory copies are avoided. Disable this to help narrow down the cause of graphical corruption.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead.name: CPU Render-Ahead
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead.tooltip: Keeps rendering in step with the game logic instead of letting the CPU queue frames ahead. This reduces input latency, at some cost to frame-rate smoothness.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: For debugging only. The maximum number of frames that may be in flight to the GPU. Changing this is not recommended: very low or high values can make frame rates unstable.
sodium.options.fps_overlay.name: FPS Overlay
sodium.options.fps_overlay.tooltip: Shows a frame-rate overlay in the corner of the screen, including your current CPU/GPU bottleneck.
